battery_100.name: Kings 100Ah Lithium Battery
battery_100.why: The cheapest well-known 100Ah, sold online by Adventure Kings with delivery Australia-wide.
battery_100.downside: Only a 1-year warranty and no app.

battery_100.name: VoltX 100Ah Lithium Battery
battery_100.why: Similar money to the Kings, bought online, with a longer warranty.
battery_100.downside: Online only, and the warranty wording on the listing is unclear, so check it before you buy.

battery_100.name: iTechworld iTECH120X PRO 120Ah
battery_100.why: An extra 20Ah, a phone app and a 5-year Aussie warranty for not much more than budget.
battery_100.downside: No heater, so it won't charge in freezing weather.

battery_100.name: Renogy 100Ah Pro (self-heating)
battery_100.why: Pick this if you camp somewhere frosty. It warms itself up before charging.

battery_100.name: REDARC REDLAB Icon 100Ah
battery_100.why: Australian brand with a built-in heater, a 5-year warranty and a charge display on the battery. Made to pair with REDARC chargers.
battery_100.downside: About three to four times the price of the budget picks for the same usable power.

battery_100.name: Enerdrive eLITE 100Ah
battery_100.why: A respected caravan-industry brand for well under REDARC money.

battery_200.name: Kings 200Ah Lithium Battery
battery_200.why: Easy to order online, and people who've opened one up say it's decent inside for the money.
battery_200.downside: No app or cold-weather heater, so check the charge on a separate monitor.

battery_200.name: Renogy Reserve Mini 200Ah
battery_200.why: Ticks every box: built-in heater, phone app, strong 205A output and a 5-year warranty. Compact and light for 200Ah.
battery_200.downside: Online only, and on pre-order until November. The iTechworld 200Ah slim is a good in-stock alternative.

battery_200.name: iTechworld iTECH200SS Super Slim
battery_200.why: Phone app, a strong 200A output and a 5-year Aussie warranty, in a slim 12.6cm shape that fits a van wall or under a seat. In stock.
battery_200.downside: No heater, so it won't charge in freezing weather. The Renogy under Other good options has one.

battery_200.name: REDARC REDLAB Icon 200Ah
battery_200.why: Australian-designed, heated, and the 5-year warranty covers work use too.
battery_200.downside: About three times the mid-range price.

battery_200.name: Enerdrive B-TEC 200Ah Gen2
battery_200.why: A long-time favourite of caravan builders, with app monitoring.
battery_200.downside: No heater, and it can take 2 to 3 weeks to arrive.

battery_400.name: 2 × Kings 200Ah Lithium
battery_400.why: The cheapest way to about 400Ah from one well-known brand.
battery_400.downside: No app or heater, and you'll need link cables to join the two.

battery_400.name: iTechworld iTECH400X PRO 400Ah
battery_400.why: One battery, one set of terminals, a phone app and 5 years' cover. Simpler than linking two.
battery_400.downside: 38kg in one lump is hard to lift into place, and there's no heater.

battery_400.name: 2 × Renogy Reserve Mini 200Ah
battery_400.why: Heated, and split into two 20kg pieces that are easier to carry and fit.
battery_400.downside: Needs link cables and an auto electrician to join them.

battery_400.name: Enerdrive B-TEC 400Ah bundle (2 × 200Ah)
battery_400.why: A proven caravan-grade brand, sold as a matched pair with the link cables.
battery_400.downside: Special order and can't be returned. No heater.

battery_400.name: 2 × REDARC REDLAB Icon 200Ah
battery_400.why: The top choice for charging in freezing weather and an all-REDARC system.

powerbox_100.name: Kings BatBlock25 with 100Ah Lithium
powerbox_100.why: Battery, 25A DC-DC, solar input, plugs and USB-C in one box, with a 7m lead to your car battery included.
powerbox_100.downside: Heavier and bulkier than separate parts, and if one part fails the whole box goes in for repair.

powerbox_100.name: iTechworld GoFurther box with 120Ah PRO
powerbox_100.why: Best value: a faster 40A charger, solar input, a battery monitor, phone app and a 5-year battery warranty.
powerbox_100.downside: Stock comes and goes, so check it's available.

powerbox_100.name: iTechworld GoFurther box with 100Ah
powerbox_100.why: The same box, if the 120Ah version is sold out.
powerbox_100.downside: Smaller battery, no app and a shorter warranty for about the same price.

powerbox_100.name: REDARC GoBlock 100Ah
powerbox_100.why: Top Australian build with a 50A charger, 50A solar regulator and full app control. Charges much faster.
powerbox_100.downside: About three and a half times the mid-range iTechworld price, with a 2-year warranty.

dcdc_25.name: Kings 25A DC-DC Charger
dcdc_25.why: The cheapest way to charge a lithium battery from both your engine and solar, with plug-in leads.
dcdc_25.downside: Kings don't publish the warranty or solar limits, so check with Adventure Kings before you buy.

dcdc_25.name: Renogy 30A DC-DC with MPPT
dcdc_25.why: A bit more charging (30A) for similar money.

dcdc_25.name: REDARC BCDC Core 25A
dcdc_25.why: Australian REDARC quality, works with smart alternators, and almost every auto electrician knows it.
dcdc_25.downside: Mounts inside the car only, not under the bonnet. No app.

dcdc_25.name: Projecta IDC25X 25A
dcdc_25.why: Fully waterproof, can go under the bonnet, and has a 5-year warranty. Also at BCF.
dcdc_25.downside: The app needs an extra display you buy separately.

dcdc_25.name: REDARC BCDC Alpha 25A
dcdc_25.why: Top-end REDARC with phone app control and solar priority, so it uses the sun before your alternator.
dcdc_25.downside: About double the Core for the same 25A of charging.

dcdc_25.name: REDARC BCDC Classic 25A
dcdc_25.why: The long-proven REDARC that can live under the bonnet.
dcdc_25.downside: No app, and it costs more than the mid-range Projecta.

dcdc_40.name: Renogy 40A DC-DC with MPPT
dcdc_40.why: Very cheap for 40A with solar built in.
dcdc_40.downside: Only takes small 12V-style panels (25V max), not big house-style panels.

dcdc_40.name: iTechworld 40A DC-DC
dcdc_40.why: Takes a wider range of panels than the Renogy and handles smart alternators.

dcdc_40.name: Kings 40A DC-DC Charger
dcdc_40.why: Easy to order online, and it plugs straight into Kings batteries and leads.
dcdc_40.downside: Costs more than the Renogy and iTechworld, and specs aren't published.

dcdc_40.name: REDARC BCDC Core 40A
dcdc_40.why: Brand-name reliability that every installer knows, at a fair price for 40A.
dcdc_40.downside: Mounts inside the car only, no app.

dcdc_40.name: REDARC BCDC Core 40A Quick Connect
dcdc_40.why: Plug-in connectors make the install simpler.
dcdc_40.downside: Same limits as the standard Core.

dcdc_40.name: Enerdrive DC2DC 40A + MPPT
dcdc_40.why: Takes up to 800W of solar and has a 5-year warranty, so you can grow your panels later. A screen shows what it's doing.

dcdc_40.name: REDARC BCDC Classic 40A
dcdc_40.why: The pick if the charger has to sit in the engine bay.
dcdc_40.downside: No app, and dearer than the Enerdrive.

dcdc_50.name: Renogy 50A DC-DC with MPPT
dcdc_50.why: The cheapest 50A with solar and a phone app, and it takes bigger panels (up to 50V).
dcdc_50.downside: Shops price it quite differently, so compare before you buy.

dcdc_50.name: Projecta IDC50X 50A
dcdc_50.why: 5-year warranty and up to 800W of solar, so it suits a roof full of panels.
dcdc_50.downside: The app needs an extra display.

dcdc_50.name: REDARC BCDC Classic 50A
dcdc_50.downside: No app, and only about $130 less than the premium Alpha.

dcdc_50.name: REDARC BCDC Alpha 50A
dcdc_50.why: App control, solar priority to go easy on your alternator, and it takes bigger panels (up to 48V).

dcdc_50.name: REDARC Alpha 50 with Smart Battery Monitor
dcdc_50.why: Charger and an accurate battery monitor in one matched kit, all in one app.
dcdc_50.downside: About $300 more than an Alpha plus a Victron SmartShunt bought separately.

dcdc_50.name: Victron Orion XS 50A (no solar input)
dcdc_50.why: An excellent, efficient charger with a built-in app, if you're going all Victron.
dcdc_50.downside: No solar input. You'd need a separate solar controller as well.

blanket_200.name: Hard Korr 200W Solar Blanket
blanket_200.why: An Aussie brand with a regulator you can unplug. Leave it off when you plug into a DC-DC charger.
blanket_200.downside: The built-in regulator is the basic type, so feed it through your DC-DC. Snowys is pickup only right now.

blanket_200.name: iTechworld 200W Solar Blanket
blanket_200.why: Tough outer cover and good local support.
blanket_200.downside: Heavier than the budget Hard Korr, with a 1-year warranty.

blanket_200.name: REDARC 160W Solar Blanket
blanket_200.why: Australian-made quality with a genuine Anderson plug, built to plug into a REDARC charger, and backed by ARB stores everywhere.
blanket_200.downside: About four times the budget Hard Korr per watt, for fewer watts.

roof_200.name: Renogy 200W N-Type Mono Panel
roof_200.why: Well-known brand, 5-year warranty, and a long narrow shape that suits van roofs.

roof_200.name: Victron 190W Mono Panel
roof_200.why: A top-quality brand for about $1 a watt, the cheapest decent fixed panel we can link to right now.

roof_200.name: REDARC 200W Black Frame Panel
roof_200.why: Australian brand that ARB stores sell and fit. Pairs neatly with a REDARC charger.
roof_200.downside: About $2 a watt, with a shorter warranty than Renogy.

roof_200.name: Sunman eArc 200W Flexible Panel
roof_200.why: Light, glass-free and low profile, for curved roofs or pop-tops.
roof_200.downside: Flexible panels run hotter stuck flat to a roof.

roof_600.name: 3 × Renogy 200W N-Type Mono Panels
roof_600.why: 5-year warranty, and the narrow shape lies across a van roof more easily.

roof_600.name: 3 × Victron 190W Mono Panels
roof_600.why: A top-quality brand for less than the mid-range Renogy setup.

roof_600.name: 3 × REDARC 200W Black Frame Panels
roof_600.why: A one-brand REDARC system with ARB fitting and support across Australia.
roof_600.downside: Nearly three times the budget price for the same watts.

roof_600.name: 3 × Sunman eArc 200W Flexible Panels
roof_600.why: The lightweight way to 600W, far less weight than glass.
roof_600.downside: Needs proper mounting with airflow underneath.

inverter_600.name: Jaycar 500W Pure Sine Inverter
inverter_600.why: Small, light and cheap, from a store with branches everywhere. Plenty for laptops and camera chargers.
inverter_600.downside: Being replaced by a newer model, so stock may run out.

inverter_600.name: Victron Phoenix 12/800
inverter_600.why: Top-quality brand and a 5-year warranty, for less than most mid-range brands.
inverter_600.downside: It's rated 800VA, which is about 650W of real output.

inverter_600.name: Projecta IP600 600W
inverter_600.why: Comes with a remote display and wiring kit, and it's easy to find at car-parts stores.
inverter_600.downside: Costs more than the Victron, which is better built.

inverter_600.name: Enerdrive ePOWER 600W
inverter_600.why: Australian RV specialist, 5-year warranty, compact at 2kg. A safety-switch (RCD) version is available.
inverter_600.downside: Handles smaller start-up surges than the mid-range Victron.

inverter_2000.name: Renogy 2000W Pure Sine (with UPS)
inverter_2000.why: A known brand at a budget price. Switches to campsite power by itself when you plug in.
inverter_2000.downside: Warranty isn't listed, so ask before buying.

inverter_2000.name: Hard Korr 2000W Pure Sine
inverter_2000.why: Aussie brand with a 2-year replacement warranty, light at 3kg, and stocked at Supercheap.

inverter_2000.name: iTechworld 2000W Pure Sine
inverter_2000.why: Good local support, often bundled with their batteries.
inverter_2000.downside: 1-year warranty and heavier than the Hard Korr.

inverter_2000.name: Enerdrive ePOWER 2000W
inverter_2000.why: Built for RVs to run coffee machines and hairdryers day after day, with a 5-year warranty. RCD versions available.
inverter_2000.downside: About two and a half times the mid-range Hard Korr.

inverter_2000.name: Victron Phoenix 12/2000 Smart
inverter_2000.why: Top build quality with a built-in app, ideal in a full Victron system.
inverter_2000.downside: Rated 2000VA, about 1,600W real output. Was sold out when we checked.

monitor.name: Kings 500A Battery Monitor
monitor.why: A wired screen showing your real battery percentage and power in and out, for about $100.
monitor.downside: No app, and no warranty listed.

monitor.name: iTechworld BM500 Monitor
monitor.why: Same job and price from an Aussie lithium specialist.

monitor.name: Renogy 500A Battery Monitor
monitor.why: Well reviewed, with low-battery alarms. Also at Supercheap.

monitor.name: Victron SmartShunt 500A
monitor.why: The accuracy and app installers trust, for only about $40 more than budget. Shows hours left on your phone.
monitor.downside: No wall screen, your phone is the display. Mount it somewhere dry.

monitor.name: Victron SmartShunt 500A
monitor.why: Same monitor from a van-build specialist.

monitor.name: Victron BMV-712 Smart
monitor.why: Everything the SmartShunt does plus a proper wall screen everyone can glance at.
monitor.downside: Needs a hole cut for the screen.

monitor.name: REDARC Smart Battery Monitor
monitor.why: Best in a REDARC setup, with everything in one app.
monitor.downside: Dearest option, and the screen is extra.

fridge_medium.name: Kings 45L Stayzcool MKII
fridge_medium.why: A proper compressor fridge-freezer with a 5-year warranty for about $750, holds about 72 cans.
fridge_medium.downside: Kings doesn't publish a lot of detail, and it's heavier than the mid-range Dometic.
fridge_medium.draw: 0.65 to 1.25Ah per hour (Kings figure, fridge at 3°C, 32°C outside, 13.2V)

fridge_medium.name: Brass Monkey 42L Ultra-Portable (Jaycar)
fridge_medium.why: On clearance for about $250 with wheels and a 3-year warranty, if you just want something cold cheaply.
fridge_medium.downside: Jaycar publishes no power use figure, it's 12/24V DC only, and stock is check-your-store.

fridge_medium.name: Dometic CFF45
fridge_medium.why: The fridge we run in our Hiace: light on power for a 45L and currently cheaper than the budget Kings while it's being cleared out.
fridge_medium.downside: Being run out, so stock is patchy and BCF/Snowys may sell out. 3-year warranty, not 5.
fridge_medium.draw: 0.88Ah per hour (Dometic figure, 5°C inside, 32°C outside, 12V); 4.5A max

fridge_medium.name: Dometic CFX5 45
fridge_medium.why: Dometic's top portable: lower power use than the mid-range CFF45, a phone app, a 5-year warranty and tougher build.
fridge_medium.downside: About double the price of the mid-range CFF45 for the same size.

fridge_medium.name: Engel MT-V45 (40L)
fridge_medium.why: Engel's swing-motor compressor has a long reputation for running for decades on rough roads.
fridge_medium.downside: Heavy (24kg), smaller inside (40L) and Snowys gives no test conditions for its power figure.
fridge_medium.draw: 0.5A to 2.6A max per hour at 12V (no test conditions given)

fridge_medium.name: Bushman 35-52L
fridge_medium.why: Clever lid swap lets it grow from 35L to 52L, and it sips power (Australian-designed).
fridge_medium.downside: Pricey and heavy at 24.5kg, and the stated compressor warranty differs between listing and staff answer.
fridge_medium.draw: 0.67Ah per hour (maker figure, -4°C inside, 25°C outside, 52L setup)

fridge_large.name: Kings 60L Stayzcool MKII
fridge_large.why: 60L with a 5-year warranty for about $850, a lot of fridge for the money.
fridge_large.downside: Kings publishes no power use figure or weight on the product page.

fridge_large.name: Dometic CFF 70DZ
fridge_large.why: Dual zone (fridge one side, freezer the other) from a big brand, heavily discounted to under $1,000 with a cover.
fridge_large.downside: Draws a fair bit with the freezer side running, and 3-year warranty.
fridge_large.draw: 2.9Ah per hour (Dometic figure, 4°C large side, -15°C small side, 32°C outside, 12V); 4A max

fridge_large.name: Kings 75L Stayzcool MKII Dual Zone
fridge_large.why: Bigger dual zone with a 5-year warranty for about $1,000.
fridge_large.downside: No published power use figure, so it's harder to size your battery.

fridge_large.name: Dometic CFX5 55
fridge_large.why: Low power use for its size, phone app and a 5-year warranty.
fridge_large.downside: Single zone, so no separate freezer side.
fridge_large.draw: 0.87Ah per hour average (Dometic figure, 4°C inside, 32°C outside, 12V); 9.6A max

fridge_large.name: Dometic CFX5 75DZ
fridge_large.why: Dual zone version with separate fridge and freezer sides that you set from your phone.
fridge_large.downside: Heavy at 27.7kg and uses close to three times the power of the single-zone 55.
fridge_large.draw: 2.45Ah per hour average (Dometic figure, 4°C large, -15°C small, 32°C outside, 12V)

fridge_large.name: Engel MT-V60
fridge_large.why: Engel's famously tough swing-motor compressor for people who want it to last decades.
fridge_large.downside: Very heavy at 33kg, and no test conditions given for the power figure.
fridge_large.draw: 0.5A to 4.2A max per hour at 12V (no test conditions given)

fridge_ff.name: Kings 90L Stayzcool MKII Dual Zone
fridge_ff.why: 90L with two zones you can set separately, and a 5-year warranty, for about $1,100.
fridge_ff.downside: No published power use figure or weight; expect it to be heavy.

fridge_ff.name: EvaKool DU295-DZ Down Under 95L
fridge_ff.why: Australian brand with a Secop compressor, low published power use for a 95L dual zone and a 5-year full warranty.
fridge_ff.downside: Heavy at 34kg, and a big footprint for a van.
fridge_ff.draw: 2.2Ah per hour (maker figure, 2°C fridge, -16°C freezer, 32°C outside, over 24h)

fridge_ff.name: EvaKool DU280-DZ Down Under 80L
fridge_ff.why: Same build in a smaller 80L size that fits more vans and uses a bit less power.
fridge_ff.draw: 2Ah per hour (maker figure, 2°C fridge, -16°C freezer, 32°C outside, over 24h)

fridge_ff.name: myCOOLMAN CCP96DZ 96L
fridge_ff.why: Australian-owned brand, 96L dual zone with a 5-year warranty.
fridge_ff.downside: Higher published power use than the EvaKool and nearly 35kg.
fridge_ff.draw: 3.1Ah per hour (maker figure, 3°C fridge, -15°C freezer, 32°C outside, 12V)

fridge_ff.name: Dometic CFX5 95DZ
fridge_ff.why: Dometic's top dual zone: phone app control, strong build and a 5-year warranty.
fridge_ff.downside: About $400 to $650 more than the mid-range EvaKool, and Snowys showed it out of stock online.
fridge_ff.draw: 2.83Ah per hour average (Dometic figure, 4°C large, -15°C small, 32°C outside, 12V); 10.4A max

lights.name: Kings 4m 12V LED Camping Strip
lights.why: A 4-metre dimmable strip with a cigarette plug for $30, easy to hang in a van or under an awning.
lights.downside: No warranty period stated and no brightness figure published.

lights.name: Kings Illuminator 4 Bar Camp Light Kit
lights.why: Four 50cm magnetic bars with extension leads and a dimmer for $50, so you can light several spots.
lights.downside: White only (no bug-friendly orange), no power or warranty figure listed.

lights.name: Hard Korr Lifestyle 4 Bar Orange/White Kit
lights.why: Australian brand with an orange mode that attracts fewer bugs, and a published 2,300 lumens.
lights.downside: Two of the bars are white only, and warranty isn't shown on the page.

lights.name: Narva 285mm White/Amber LED Strip Light
lights.why: A fixed, sealed light you screw inside the van or under the awning, with a bug-friendly amber mode.
lights.downside: Needs wiring in with a separate switch, so get an auto electrician to fit it. 1-year warranty.

lights.name: Hard Korr 6 Bar Tri-Colour Camp Light Kit
lights.why: Every bar does cool white, warm white or orange, with 6 bars and lots of leads to light a whole camp, plus a 5-year replacement warranty.
lights.downside: Overkill for inside a small van, and Hard Korr's own store shows it sold out.

lights.name: Hard Korr 4 Bar Tri-Colour Camp Light Kit
lights.why: Same tri-colour bars and 5-year warranty in a smaller kit that suits a van or small camp.
lights.downside: Only $30 less than the 6 bar at current Snowys prices.

fans.name: Rovin 12V Oscillating Clamp Fan 6"
fans.why: Clamps on anywhere and plugs into a 12V socket, for about $33.
fans.downside: No official power figure (staff estimate under 7W), 1-year warranty.
fans.draw: about 7W or less (staff estimate, not a spec)

fans.name: Kings 2in1 Rechargeable LED Light/Fan
fans.why: Cordless with a built-in battery and light, charged by USB-C, so no wiring at all.
fans.downside: Runs about 6 hours on full, and no warranty period stated.
fans.draw: USB-C rechargeable; up to 25h on low, 6h on high

fans.name: Rovin Dual 100mm 12V Clamp Fans
fans.why: Two fan heads on one clamp, so you can point air at two people in bed.

fans.name: Caframo Sirocco II 12/24V Fan
fans.why: The quiet, very low-power fan many caravanners fit; it folds flat and swivels in any direction.
fans.downside: Needs screwing to a wall or ceiling and wiring to 12V, ideally by an auto electrician.

fans.name: MaxxAir MaxxFan Deluxe (power lift, remote, 355mm)
fans.why: A roof vent fan that pulls hot air out or brings cool air in, with a thermostat, remote and a rain dome so it can run in the rain.
fans.downside: Needs a 355mm square hole in the roof, sealing and wiring, so it's a professional install. Only 1-year warranty on Australian stock.

fans.name: Fiamma Turbo-Vent fan kit (for Vent 28 F)
fans.why: If your van already has a Fiamma Vent 28 F hatch, this adds a 12V fan for far less than a MaxxFan.
fans.downside: Fan kit only, it needs the Fiamma Vent 28 F hatch, no rain dome, 1-year warranty.

box_100.name: Powertech Battery Box with Power Accessories (HB8504)
box_100.why: A cheap, light plastic box for a battery up to 100Ah, with two 50A Anderson plugs, a 12V socket, USB-A and USB-C, a voltmeter and a 16A circuit breaker.
box_100.downside: Basic plastic and a webbing strap, so it needs tying down well in a moving vehicle. No warranty period listed.

box_100.name: KT Solar Battery Box Quad Connect (KT71201)
box_100.why: Four 50A Anderson-style ports instead of two, plus 12V sockets and USB, for about $50 more. Handy if you plug in solar, a fridge and a charger at once.
box_100.downside: No warranty or weight listed, and internal size isn't published, so measure your battery first.

box_100.name: Mean Mother Portable 12V Battery Box + Bluetooth Monitor (MMPB01)
box_100.why: Comes with an app battery monitor, so you can see charge on your phone, plus two 50A Anderson plugs on 60A fuses.
box_100.downside: 1-year warranty, and it doesn't list which battery sizes fit beyond internal size 338 x 220 x 206mm.

box_100.name: iTechworld GoFurther Premium Battery Box (with BM500 monitor)
box_100.why: A tougher box that takes batteries up to 360 x 174 x 234mm (most 100 to 120Ah lithiums), with a 175A Anderson for an inverter, four 50A Andersons, USB-C and a battery monitor with shunt.
box_100.downside: No built-in charger, and a reviewer says the inner bracket only suits a few battery sizes. Warranty period isn't shown on the page.

box_100.name: Hardkorr Heavy Duty Battery Box (HKPBATTBOXB)
box_100.why: A similar job for about $100 less: fire-rated ABS case, 200A isolator switch, four 50A Andersons and a 175A Anderson, with a 2-year replacement warranty.
box_100.downside: Max battery 330 x 180 x 240mm, so many 120Ah lithiums are a tight fit. No monitor included.

box_100.name: MSA 4X4 Battery Box Large (40018)
box_100.why: A proper bolt-down 2mm powder-coated steel box for a permanent install in a drawer system or canopy, with foam padding, bolt-down saddles and a plate to mount your DC-DC charger. Lifetime guarantee.
box_100.downside: Heavy at 11kg, has no outlets, and fitting it needs drilling (a reviewer also needed rivnuts). Internal size 330 x 244 x 194mm.

box_200.name: ORD Universal Battery Tray for 200Ah Lithium
box_200.why: A universal tray (not tied to one battery brand) in 2mm zinc-coated, powder-coated steel with two load-rated cam-buckle straps. Takes batteries up to 492 x 175mm at the base.
box_200.downside: Out of stock when checked, and no warranty listed. Too narrow for wider 200Ah batteries.

box_200.name: Invicta Battery Tray to suit 200Ah Battery
box_200.why: The matching tray for Invicta's SNL12V200BT 200Ah battery, if that's the battery you bought.
box_200.downside: Only for Invicta batteries, and no size or material is listed.

box_200.name: Cobra Large Caravan Battery Box for 200Ah Lithium
box_200.why: For caravans and camper trailers: a steel and aluminium box that mounts underneath and keeps a 200Ah battery out of the weather. In a van, a bolt-down tray does the job.
box_200.downside: Internal size isn't listed (outer 600 x 260 x 240mm), so check your battery fits. Mounting details and warranty aren't stated. A knob and nut hold it shut, not a lock.

box_200.name: Roadking Weld-On Battery Box 200Amp
box_200.why: For trailers and camper chassis: a steel box that welds on, with an aluminium slide-down lid and a long internal space (715 x 190 x 250).
box_200.downside: Must be welded on by a fabricator, and it was sold out when checked. No warranty listed.

box_200.name: REDARC 200Ah REDLAB Icon Lithium Battery Tray (LBATN12200-MB)
box_200.why: The matching galvanised tray and heavy-duty strap for the REDARC Icon 200Ah, our premium battery pick. It bolts down with four fasteners.
box_200.downside: Only fits the REDARC Icon200. It costs less than the other tiers because it's just a tray, not a box.

install_kit.name: Jaycar Premium DC-DC Wiring Kit (HB8507)
install_kit.why: 6 metres of 8 B&S cable, an 80A fuse and a 3-pin Anderson plug that carries the ignition wire many newer cars need, plus a 3m ignition lead. Good for a 25A charger.
install_kit.downside: Jaycar lists both 50A and 80A ratings, which don't match. No warranty period stated.

install_kit.name: Hardkorr Dual Battery Wiring Kit with Midi Fuse (HKPBATTWIR2)
install_kit.why: 6 metres of twin 8AWG (10mm2) cable with a 60A midi fuse, an Anderson plug and ring lugs, good for a 25A DC-DC charger with the battery in the back.
install_kit.downside: Rated 50A max and made for a VSR, so it needs adapting for a DC-DC charger. No ignition wire, which many smart-alternator vehicles need. 1-year warranty.

install_kit.name: Drivetech 4x4 DC-DC Wiring Kit 5m (DT-02022W5)
install_kit.why: Thicker 6 B&S (16mm2) tinned copper cable, which resists corrosion and loses less power, with two midi fuse holders (40A and 60A fuses), two Anderson plugs and a negative block. Suits 25A to 40A chargers.
install_kit.downside: 5m may be too short for a long wheelbase or a trailer. It is ordered in (3 to 7 business days). No warranty listed.

install_kit.name: Home of 12V Wiring Kit for DC-DC Chargers (DBK-DC)
install_kit.why: Made for 25A DC-DC chargers like the Redarc BCDC Core 25 and Projecta 25A: 6m of 8 B&S twin cable plus two 3m single runs, two 60A midi fuses with holders, lugs, heatshrink and an Anderson plug.
install_kit.downside: 8 B&S suits a 25A charger. For a 40A charger or a long run, ask your auto electrician about thicker cable. No warranty listed.

install_kit.name: Hardkorr 40A DC-DC Charger Wiring Kit (HKPDCDCWIRM40)
install_kit.why: About $45 less: 6.5m of 6AWG cable, a 60A midi fuse, a 3-pin Anderson plug with ignition wire and a 3m wire for smart alternators. 2-year replacement warranty.

install_kit.name: REDARC BCDC 50A Rear Install Wiring Kit (BCDCWK-006)
install_kit.why: REDARC's own kit for its 40A and 50A BCDC chargers with the battery at the other end of the vehicle (up to 8.5m). Pre-crimped cables, terminal block, fuses and conduit, so an auto electrician fits it quickly.
install_kit.downside: Pricey, and only matched to REDARC BCDC1240D/1250D. Battery earth cable and solar cable are sold separately.

install_kit.name: REDARC BCDC Alpha 50A Rear Install Wiring Kit (BCDCWK-108)
install_kit.why: The matching kit for the newer BCDC Alpha 50 charger, about $100 less, with 60A midi fuses and pre-crimped cables for runs up to 6.5m.
install_kit.downside: Only for BCDC Alpha 50A chargers. Cable sizes are only listed in the manual.

fuse_block.name: Narva 6-Way ATS Blade Fuse Box (54422BL)
fuse_block.why: A simple fuse box so each 12V item (fridge, lights, USB) has its own fuse. Takes up to 30A per circuit, with a clear sealed cover.
fuse_block.downside: No negative bus, so you need a separate earth point. Pair it with an isolator switch and a main fuse at the battery.

fuse_block.name: Blue Sea ST Blade Fuse Block 6 Circuit with Negative Bus (5025)
fuse_block.why: A marine-grade fuse block that installers trust, rated 100A total, with a built-in negative bus so positives and earths land in one tidy place.
fuse_block.downside: Only 6 circuits. Still needs a main fuse and an isolator switch.

fuse_block.name: Enerdrive 12-Way Blade Fuse Block with Negative Busbar (EA-FB-07)
fuse_block.why: Double the circuits of the Blue Sea for a similar price (100A total, 30A per circuit), with a negative busbar and a 5-year warranty. Good for a bigger build.
fuse_block.downside: Bigger to mount, and low stock at both stores when checked.

fuse_block.name: Blue Sea SafetyHub 150 Fuse Block (7748)
fuse_block.why: All the fusing in one sealed (IP66) box: four MIDI fuses up to 200A for big items like the inverter and DC-DC charger, six blade fuses for small circuits, and a negative bus.
fuse_block.downside: Costs about three times a basic block, and you still need an isolator switch. Stores list different total ratings (200A vs 280A at 12V).

isolator.name: Narva 100A Rotary Battery Master Switch (61036BL)
isolator.why: A compact on/off isolator with a removable key, so you can cut all power from the house battery when parked or working on it.
isolator.downside: Only 100A, fine for fridges and lights but too small for a big inverter. No warranty listed.

isolator.name: Blue Sea m-Series Mini On-Off Battery Switch (6006)
isolator.why: The isolator to pair with it: rated 300A continuous, so it copes with an inverter, and small enough to fit in a van or canopy.
isolator.downside: Single circuit on/off only, with no key lock.

isolator.name: Narva Heavy Duty Battery Master Switch 300A IP67 (61044BL)
isolator.why: A sealed, heavy-duty isolator rated 300A continuous (1000A for 5 seconds), so it suits exposed spots like a ute tray or under a trailer.
isolator.downside: Pricier than the mid-range Blue Sea switch for the same continuous rating. No warranty listed.
